title: Parts of Speech
description: Identifying parts of speech in context. Starts with nouns, verbs, and adjectives (grade 3), adds adverbs and pronouns (grade 4), then prepositions, conjunctions, and interjections (grades 5-6).
subject: language-arts
source: Common Core ELA grammar standards L.3.1, L.4.1, L.5.1. Sentences drafted for this pack.

items.prompt: In the sentence 'The happy dog barked loudly,' which word is a NOUN?
items.context: A noun is a person, place, thing, or idea.

items.prompt: In the sentence 'The happy dog barked loudly,' which word is a VERB?
items.context: A verb is an action or state of being.

items.prompt: In the sentence 'The happy dog barked loudly,' which word is an ADJECTIVE?
Which word is a NOUN?
Which word is a VERB?
Which word is an ADJECTIVE?
In 'She has three sisters,' which word is the NOUN?
In 'The baby cried all night,' which word is the VERB?
In 'She ran quickly across the field,' which word is an ADVERB?
items.context: An adverb describes a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. It often tells how, when, where, or to what degree. Many end in -ly.

items.prompt: In 'The bird sang beautifully,' which word is an ADVERB?
Which word is a PRONOUN?
items.context: A pronoun replaces a noun. Examples: he, she, it, they, we, you, I, me, him, her, them, us.

items.prompt: In 'They gave us the keys,' which word is NOT a pronoun?
Which word is an ADVERB?
In 'The old man walked slowly,' which word is the ADVERB?
In 'The book is on the table,' which word is a PREPOSITION?
items.context: A preposition shows a relationship of location, time, or direction between words. Common ones: on, in, under, over, to, from, with, between, through.

items.prompt: In 'We walked through the park,' which word is a PREPOSITION?
In 'I like apples and oranges,' which word is a CONJUNCTION?
items.context: A conjunction joins words, phrases, or clauses. Common ones: and, but, or, so, because, if, when, although.

items.prompt: In 'She wanted to go, but it was raining,' which word is a CONJUNCTION?
Which word is a PREPOSITION?
Which word is a CONJUNCTION?
In 'Wow! That was amazing,' what part of speech is WOW?
items.context: An interjection is a word that expresses strong emotion and often stands alone. Examples: wow, ouch, hey, oh, yikes.

items.prompt: In 'The cat that I adopted is friendly,' what part of speech is THAT?
items.context: Here THAT is a relative pronoun introducing a clause about the cat.

items.prompt: In 'Running is good exercise,' what part of speech is RUNNING?
items.context: RUNNING looks like a verb, but here it is a gerund, which is a verb form acting as a noun. You can tell because it's the subject of the sentence.

items.prompt: In 'She sings very well,' what part of speech is VERY?
items.context: VERY is an adverb modifying another adverb (well). Adverbs can modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
